doc.title: Earl May interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 11, 2001

chapter: Mingus, road life and the jazz economy
title: Road work, four marriages and traveling with his wife
summary: May jokes about being married four times and the effect of touring; his present wife travels with him, as to Paris.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Meeting, courting and marrying: musicians' love lives

blocks.x: How much road work was involved in your—
Well you’d have to ask — I’ve been married four times. You’d have to ask my other three wives.

I think what happens is that they think it’s kind of a nice life, and they want to be with me, but I’m not there. On weekends I’m not home, on holidays I’m not home. So it gets kind of really — I come in at night, “Earl is that you?” Like it’s kind of frightening you know. But we’re all good friends, I mean all my ex-wives call the house everyday. As a matter of fact this week alone I’ve spoken to, well everybody, all my ex-wives. They all call my house. My wife is good friends with everybody. They say, “Is he still doing—” something. “Yeah, yeah, yeah.”
Did they ever try going with you?

Not the others like as much as my present wife. She just goes, “Yeah, come on, let’s go.” And she jumps right on it. She rearranges her work schedule so that she can be with me. We just went to Paris the latter part of last year. Had a wonderful time. It was just like being on a honeymoon. Because I really miss that. I mean it’s wonderful to share some of the things that I’ve gone through with someone that you really love. It’s wonderful. I just get tickled every time I think about that.
